title: Runner multi-repo phase 4: strip apiary-specific rules from auto_plan prompt
problem: auto_plan.build_prompt hardcodes apiary-specific guidance into every plan-stage prompt: 'ALWAYS read CLAUDE.md (project root) and docs/standards/code-style.md', 'stdlib only (no external dependencies), use unittest (no pytest)', 'pathlib.Path end-to-end', 'no shell=True', 'no absolute paths', the runner-package import convention, and a BANNED TOKENS list (`pytest`, `shell=true`, `import requests`) that validate_plan.py auto-rejects on. validate_plan also enforces that banned-token list. After phases 1-3 land, a runner pass against a Node project, a Rust project, or any non-apiary repo will get a plan that proposes Python unittest, then have the planner forced into stdlib-only Python conventions, then have its plan rejected by the validator's banned-tokens check. Phase 4 makes the rules target-aware so the runner can plan correctly for whatever conventions the target repo follows.
description: Refactor auto_plan.build_prompt to stop embedding apiary-specific rules. Instead, at plan time, read the target repo's CLAUDE.md (if present) and any conventional standards docs (e.g. docs/standards/, CONTRIBUTING.md, AGENTS.md — the exact set is TBD; start with CLAUDE.md only and expand if needed) and inject them into the prompt as 'Target repo conventions' context. Make validate_plan.py's banned-token list configurable per target via runner/config.json (e.g. `runner.target_overrides.<key>.banned_tokens`), defaulting to the current apiary-specific list when no override is configured AND target == apiary, and to an empty list otherwise. Provide a fixture non-apiary target repo (could be a tiny scratch repo under tests/fixtures/) and a regression test that exercises auto_plan + validate_plan end-to-end against it without any apiary-isms leaking through. Confirm apiary-self runner behavior is unchanged (same prompt body, same banned-tokens enforcement) — this should be a pure refactor for the apiary case.
scope: runner/auto_plan.py (build_prompt: read target CLAUDE.md, drop hardcoded rules, inject as context), runner/validate_plan.py (banned-token list becomes config-driven), runner/config.json (schema for per-target overrides + apiary defaults), tests/fixtures/<scratch-target-repo>/ (or equivalent), runner/test_auto_plan.py and runner/test_validate_plan.py regression coverage for both apiary-self and the fixture target. Acceptance: (a) running auto_plan + validate_plan against the apiary-self path produces byte-identical prompt output and validator behavior to pre-refactor; (b) running against the fixture target produces a prompt with the fixture's CLAUDE.md content (not apiary's) and the validator does NOT reject plans containing the word 'pytest' if the fixture's config does not ban it. OUT OF SCOPE: changing auto_refine's prompt (separate concern — refine doesn't enforce conventions, only describes), changing executor's prompt body, changing the harden stage prompt, supporting any standards-doc paths beyond a single CLAUDE.md (CONTRIBUTING.md, AGENTS.md, etc. can be follow-ups).
context: Part of the runner multi-repo rearchitecture epic agreed in session 27d1126d (2026-04-16). Final phase of the epic. Phase 1 (in-session) introduces target-repo-aware worktrees; phase 2 makes stages load runner code from apiary regardless of cwd; phase 3 adds the operator-facing CLI flag + intake field; this phase 4 makes the planner stop assuming target == apiary. Without this ticket, multi-repo runs will produce plans that look apiary-flavored regardless of the target. Depends on phases 1-3 landing first.
